newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: CPC awards leaded reformate, delays unleaded.
newsitem.headline: CPC awards leaded reformate, delays unleaded.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) has awarded its tender to buy leaded 95-octane reformate but will only award its unleaded tender on Wednesday, a company official said on Tuesday.
The official said the leaded cargo was awarded at $25.20 per barrel on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis to Keelung, Taichung, Kaohsiung or Shalung.

The tender, which closed April 21 and is valid for two days, sought a 250,000-barrel cargo of unleaded reformate for delivery May 16-31 and/or June 1-15 and a 250,000-barrel cargo of leaded reformate for June 1-15 arrival.
"The number is not so good," the official said on the unleaded offers. "We have asked the sellers to recounter their offers."

In its last tender for May 1-15 delivery, CPC bought two unleaded cargoes at $27.40 per barrel, c-and-f, from South Korean refiner Yukong and Dutch trader Vitol, and an unleaded cargo from Swiss trader Glencore at $27.70.
